As of October 20, 2025, the “purity” of Anniversary Realms is effectively gone in both economy and botting. The fresh start dream was quickly compromised, and here’s the hard data and on-the-ground reality:

  1. Economy: Already Inflated & Exploited
  • Gold prices are through the roof:
    • On high-pop realms 1,000 gold = $8–12 USD on third-party sites.
    • Epic crafting mats (e.g., Arcanite, Mooncloth) are hoarded and price-gouged by bot networks.
  • Auction house dominated by bot farmers:
    • Herbalism/Alchemy bots flood the market with Dreamfoil, Black Lotus, etc.
    • Fishing bots control Stonescale Eel and Deviate Fish pools.
    • Layer-hopping bots farm DM East jump runs 24/7 — selling Tribute runs for 50–100g each.

Proof: Wowhead economy trackers and Saddlebag Exchange show Black Lotus at 80–120g on most realms — up from 30g at launch. That’s not organic demand — that’s bot supply manipulation.

  1. Botting: Rampant & Unchecked
  • Bot density is higher than Classic 2019 launch:
    • Mage AOE farmers in ZF, DM North, BRD — entire zones cleared by scripts.
    • Warlock bots with succubus kiting in Felwood and Blasted Lands.
    • Druid bots in Dire Maul East — 100+ accounts per server reported.
  • Blizzard’s response? Minimal.
    • Ban waves are reactive, not preventive.
    • Botters use VPNs, fresh accounts ($5 each), and gold laundering — back online in hours.
    • No hardware ID bans (unlike Retail) — Classic uses legacy systems.

Community reports: Reddit’s r/classicwow and WoW forums are flooded with screenshots:

  • “50 mages in ZF at 3 AM”
  • “Same bot name pattern: XxHerb123, XxHerb124…”
  • Guilds openly selling boosts for PayPal
  1. Boosting: Professional & Organized
  • Boosting guilds run like businesses:
    • Zul’Farak, Stockades, SM boosts — 5–10g per run.
    • Maraudon, BRD, LBRS — 20–40g.
    • Layer manipulation + multi-boxing = 100+ boosts per hour.
  • Payment via Discord, PayPal, crypto — zero Blizzard oversight.
  • Top boosters earn $1,000+/week — tax-free.
  1. Blizzard’s “Purity” Argument is Hollow They said: “We want players to experience the journey together from the start. Allowing paid services too early undermines that.” — Ion Hazzikostas (Game Director), 2024 Dev Interview

But:

  • Bots transferred in via new accounts — no restriction.
  • Gold buyers skipped the grind — paying $50 for what should take 50 hours.
  • Boosted characters hit 60 in 3 days — not 3 weeks.

The fresh experience was over by Week 2.

What Could Fix It? (But Won’t Happen)

Solution Why It Would Help Why Blizzard Won’t Do It
Enable paid faction changes Cuts demand for RMT alts “Breaks purity”
Allow realm transfers (with gold cap) Balances populations “Undermines fresh start”
Free name changes + appearance changes Reduces need to reroll Minor revenue loss
Hardware bans + IP tracking Stops bot recycling Legacy code limitations
Cross-faction dungeons/raids Fixes pop imbalance “Not authentic to Vanilla”

The Real Truth Blizzard sacrificed player experience for ideology — and lost control anyway.

  • Bots won.
  • Gold sellers won.
  • Legit players lost time, fairness, and fun.

The “purity” was a myth. The only thing preserved was Blizzard’s refusal to adapt.

Options (Realistic Ones)

  1. Play smart: Farm early, sell to the inflated economy.
  2. Join a guild that boosts — if you can’t beat ‘em…
  3. Wait for Phase 2 (TBC) — bots spread out, economy stabilizes.

Bottom Line: The Anniversary Realms are not fresh. They’re bot-farmed, gold-inflated, boost-heavy servers wearing a “fresh” label. Blizzard’s rules didn’t protect purity — they enabled the black market.
